newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo dinar recovers, further gains expected.
newsitem.headline: Yugo dinar recovers, further gains expected.

text.p: Yugoslavia's dinar recouped some of its holiday losses to stand at 4.0 to the mark on Friday as cash supply on the streets ebbed, dealers said.
"There are not so many dinars on the streets any longer, and we expect the dinar to strengthen a little more," one street dealer told Reuters.
The dinar black market rate stood at 4.2 to the mark on Thursday. On December 31, the dinar was changing hands at a rate of 3.8 to the mark.
The plunge in the Yugoslav currency started during the eight-day New Year and Christmas holidays, when banks and companies were closed.
Economists and financial analysts said the dinar dived to as low as 4.3 on a sudden flood of notes put into circulation during the last few days of 1996.
Some economists blamed the Serbian government for putting pressure on the National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) to resort to the presses and print money to ensure pensions were payed.
Others said the money was needed to cover huge imbalances of the two largest commercial banks.
Analysts estimated between 500 million and one billion dinars were printed for those purposes.
Some insisted it was the debtors lobby attempting to push the dinar down and erase its liabilities.
Yugoslavia's government, in its 1997 economic policy paper, pledged currency stability and the dinar fixed at 3.3 to the mark.
Sources close to the federal government and the NBY said they were scheduled to meet on Friday to discuss the latest monetary developments and the dinar's misfortune.
The government and the central bank are expected to issue statements later in the day.
In the meantime, Serbia's government said there were no economic reasons for the dinar destabilisation or devaluation.
But in a statement carried by the local media, Serbia's government did not comment on an evident monetary expansion that took place over the holidays.
Yugoslav Deputy Prime Minister Jovan Zebic told state radio he believed the dinar black rate would return very quickly to its pre-holiday level.
"The (dinar) rate is out of balance but we believe it's partly a result of various circumstances and I am sure the rate will return to below 4.0 (to the mark) within days," Zebic said.
Zebic added that dinar stability remained an important aim of 1997 economic policy. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
